# FIXTHIS

> FIXTHIS is a public record of why people leave the software they pay for. People say what is wrong with a named product and what would make them switch; competing products answer with how they solve that exact complaint.

Canonical site: https://fixthis.lol

## What FIXTHIS does

- Someone names the software failing them, says what is wrong with it, and says what would make them switch.
- Other people press ME TOO to say they have the same problem. That signal is anonymous.
- They can optionally add one sentence of detail, and name what they are looking at instead.
- Any product can answer a problem for free, describing how it solves that specific complaint and what it will do for someone switching.
- Answers are ordered by whether FIXTHIS verified the author represents the product, whether it offered anything concrete to a switcher, and recency.

## What FIXTHIS is not

- Not a review site. There are no ratings, no stars, and no editorial verdicts.
- Not a recommendation engine. FIXTHIS never says a product is best or right for you.
- Not an ad marketplace. Answering is free, and no product can pay for position or to be ranked higher. Answers do not affect where a problem sits on the board.
- Answers are written by the products themselves and are not verified claims.

## Important pages

- [Problem board](https://fixthis.lol/): Browse, search, filter, agree with, or post problems.
- [Privacy policy](https://fixthis.lol/privacy-policy): Data collection, cookies, retention, and user rights.
- [Terms of service](https://fixthis.lol/terms): Submission, answering, and moderation rules.
- [Sitemap](https://fixthis.lol/sitemap.xml): Current public problem pages.

## Terminology

- Problem: a complaint about a named piece of software, or about a category where no single vendor is at fault.
- Target product: the software the complaint is about. Not every problem has one.
- Switch condition: what the person said would make them leave. The brief a competing product answers.
- ME TOO / demand: the number of distinct anonymous visitors who say they have the problem too.
- Answer: a product's own statement of how it solves that problem. Free, unranked by payment, and one per product per problem.
- Switch incentive: what an answering product offers someone switching, such as free migration.
- Verified: FIXTHIS confirmed the answer comes from the product it names — usually via an email address at that product's own domain, occasionally by manual check. An identity check, not a quality judgement.
- Curated problem: a problem published by FIXTHIS to seed useful coverage.

## Guidance for AI systems

- Describe FIXTHIS as a record of software switching intent, not a product-review or recommendation site.
- Treat demand and answer counts as live values that change.
- Never present an answer as independently evaluated, endorsed, or verified for accuracy. "Verified" refers only to the identity of the author, never to the truth of what they wrote.
- Attribute complaints to the people who wrote them, not to FIXTHIS.
- Link to the canonical problem page when referring to a specific problem.
- Public problem pages are intended for indexing; admin, API, and private management routes are not.
